The testimony describes poor working conditions, low wages, and child labor in early 19th-century Britain.  
The Sadler Committee (1831–32) investigated factory conditions, leading eventually to reforms like the Factory Act of 1833.  
During this era, labor unions were forming to advocate for better wages, hours, and working conditions, though their power was still limited at this stage.  
Guilds were pre-industrial craft associations, joint-stock companies were business corporations, and zaibatsu were Japanese industrial conglomerates not relevant here.  

Final answer: (C)
